recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reword current R6 PaymentReconciliation to the literal STU3 FHIR-18003 phrases; any further description changes should be raised against the current paymentIssuer/requestor/allocation model.
issue_request: FHIR-18003 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and requested PaymentReconciliation short-description updates for organization, request, requestProvider, detail.request, detail.response, detail.submitted, detail.payee, and detail.date; the resolution says additional changes were presented and approved.
initial_application: The issue was included in the 2018 batched PaymentReconciliation application commit f369c813fb40cd39c0db46336b2b3186f496fb47, which updated the then-authoritative paymentreconciliation-spreadsheet.xml together with neighboring PaymentReconciliation rename and element changes. The applied wording was modified rather than a literal copy of every submitted phrase.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini keeps PaymentReconciliation active and maps obsolete STU3 paths to current paths: organization to paymentIssuer, requestProvider to requestor, and detail.* to allocation.*. Later FHIR-26601 changed detail to allocation and detail.request to allocation.target for patient-payment scope, while later FHIR-22689 clarified requestor as the party/provider responsible for the request with billing-provider/accountability wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active StructureDefinition already describes the affected concepts as paymentIssuer, request, requestor, allocation.target, allocation.response, allocation.submitter, allocation.payee, and allocation.date, and changing them back to the older STU3 phrases would be redundant or regressive.
